riskFactors.title: High Sodium Diet
riskFactors.description: Global average salt intake (10.8g/day) is double the WHO recommended limit of 5g/day.

riskFactors.title: Obesity & Overweight
riskFactors.description: Excess body weight increases vascular resistance and renal sodium retention.

riskFactors.title: Physical Inactivity
riskFactors.description: Sedentary lifestyle increases vascular stiffness and Resting Heart Rate.

riskFactors.title: High Alcohol Intake
riskFactors.description: Chronic excessive alcohol consumption directly elevates blood pressure.

riskFactors.title: Ageing Population
riskFactors.description: Arterial stiffness increases sharply after age 50.

riskFactors.title: Chronic Stress
riskFactors.description: Sustained elevation of cortisol and sympathetic drive increases resting blood pressure.

riskFactors.title: Sleep Apnea (OSA)
riskFactors.description: Obstructive sleep apnea triggers nocturnal hypertension and resistant blood pressure.

riskFactors.title: Excess Salt & Sodium
riskFactors.description: High dietary sodium intake drives fluid retention and vascular stiffness.

didYouKnow: Hypertension is known as the 'Silent Killer' because 46% of adults with high BP don't know they have it.
Only 21% of hypertensive adults globally have their blood pressure controlled under 140/90 mmHg.
Scaling up hypertension treatment globally could avert 76 million deaths between 2023 and 2050.
Reducing global salt intake by 30% could save an estimated 7 million lives by 2030.

faq.q: What blood pressure reading is considered hypertension?
faq.a: According to WHO guidelines, hypertension is diagnosed when systolic blood pressure is ≥ 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure is ≥ 90 mmHg on two separate days.

faq.q: How many people have high blood pressure worldwide?
faq.a: An estimated 1.33 billion adults aged 30–79 have hypertension worldwide, doubling from 650 million in 1990.
